correctness.rationale: For each s>=0 the 2-faces of C∩L_s are the nonzero-area sections of the 40 coordinate cube 3-faces; every such 2-face is counted exactly once even at s=0,2,4. Independent uniform-convolution/coarea calculations yield the two slice-area formulas and the exact three-branch expression. The lower bound follows by direct strict estimates on [0,1], [1,2], [2,4], and [4,infinity). Global upper and stationary points follow from an explicitly factored critical-point equation with the false squared root excluded, and a strictly negative derivative for s>1 outside the two known critical points. The saved exact-rational checker independently reconstructs 40 slice polygons at each of 18 rational s; it is finite corroboration rather than proof for all real s.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Finite-s positive-coefficient hyperplane sections are generally nonorthogonal. When s>=4 the section is an oblique parallelotope, not an orthotope; its active facet distances are strictly above one. In 0<s<4 the section is not an orthotope and similarly has facets with distance above one. Thus the special-class theorems do not imply its sharp 96 bound, much less its exact metric profile. The general 2026 result concerns surface area (dimension three) rather than dimension-two ridges.

value.rationale: The research question is directly motivated by Conjecture 5.2 of Zwierzyński (2026), with dimension four its first open case. The natural one-parameter slice family continuously interpolates a known octahedral-product endpoint and increasingly cube-like oblique four-parallelotopes. The result establishes the conjectured sharp 96 bound on an entire new infinite family not subsumed by Proposition 5.3, gives complete metric face-area classification, identifies phase transitions and nonmonotone stationary points. The claim is not a general 4D theorem.
